subject: general
question: Which feature of the Indian Constitution refers to the existence of governments at the state level and at the Centre?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Federalism.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Federalism- **

 
 
• It Is a **system of government** in which powers have been **divided between the center and the state.**
 
• There are two types of federation:**-**__**Holding together federation, Coming together federation**__**.**__
 
• The Constitution establishes a **dual polity** consisting of the Union at the Centre and the states at the **periphery.**
 
• **Powers and functions** of each tier of government are **specified and guaranteed** by the **constitution** i.e.__ **Division of Power**.__
 
• India has a **bi-cameral legislature** and it is an essential feature of federalism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The **Supreme Court** has been given the power to **settle disputes** between central and state governments.
 
• Federalism was introduced into modern India by the government of India Act of 1919.
 
• **Secularism:-**
 
 
• It is the principle of separation of the state from religious institutions.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary system-**
 
 
• ** It **is a form of government where **executives hold the power** with the **majority support** of the legislature.
